title: Environmental Awareness and Model Behaviour
description: The TDPO learns how environmental forces act on the vessel, how the DP model interprets and responds to those forces, and how to predict thruster behaviour before it happens. Professional standard means the TDPO can predict which thrusters will respond to a given force before adding it, and can explain what the current vector actually represents.

tasks.title: Environment Introduction — Progressive Build
tasks.setup: Vessel on DP in calm conditions. Record baseline thruster output for all units — this is your zero reference. Before adding each stage, write down your prediction of which thrusters will increase and by how much.
tasks.execute: Add environmental conditions in three stages. Stage 1: wind 8kts at 037 degrees. Let settle 3 minutes. Record thruster response. Compare to prediction. Stage 2: add current 0.3kts at 090 degrees. Let settle 3 minutes. Record changes. Compare to prediction. Stage 3: add wave 1.0m at 048 degrees. Let settle 3 minutes. Record changes. Compare to prediction.
professional_standard: Accurate prediction of which thrusters increase before each stage
Correct identification of dominant force at each stage
Explanation of why specific thrusters responded
Current vector reading compared to set conditions

debrief_questions: Which thruster increased most when you added wind — and does its position on the vessel explain why?
Why did the current vector reading change when you added actual current, even though the tidal current was already there?
What is the combined environmental force vector direction given wind from 037, wave from 048, and current from 090?
How does wave loading differ from wind loading in terms of how the DP responds to it?

variants.title: Adverse Environment Build
variants.note_to_tdpo: Higher forces — predictions need to account for potential saturation. Watch which thruster hits its limit first.

tasks.title: Minimum Power Heading
tasks.setup: Set environment as specified. Allow 5 minutes to settle. Record total thruster demand at current heading — this is your baseline.
tasks.execute: Test four different headings spaced 45 degrees apart. Hold each heading for 3 minutes and record total thruster demand. Find the heading that gives minimum total demand. Hold that heading for 5 minutes and confirm it is stable.
professional_standard: Test minimum four headings systematically
Correctly identify minimum power heading
Achieve measurable demand reduction from starting heading
Hold minimum power heading stably for 5 minutes

variants.title: Minimum Power Heading — Heavy Weather
variants.note_to_tdpo: Higher forces make heading selection more critical. The difference in demand between best and worst heading will be much larger.

tasks.title: Environmental Ramp to Saturation
tasks.setup: Vessel on DP in calm conditions. Enable Ramp mode for wind and wave. Set wind target 35kts at 037 degrees, wave target 3.0m at 048 degrees.
tasks.execute: Start the ramp and allow conditions to increase gradually. Monitor thruster loading continuously. Record at what wind speed the first thruster reaches saturation. Record at what point position footprint begins to degrade. Record at what point you would recommend to the OIM that operations should be reviewed.
professional_standard: Identify first saturation before position degrades
Correct identification of which thruster saturates first
Reasoned recommendation point with evidence
Understanding of relationship between saturation and position accuracy

debrief_questions: Which thruster saturated first and does its position on the vessel explain why it was first?
At what sea state would you recommend the OIM consider changing heading or suspending operations on this vessel?
What is a capability plot and how would it have predicted what you just observed in this exercise?
What is the relationship between thruster saturation and position keeping accuracy — why does one cause the other?

variants.title: Ramp at Non-Optimal Heading
variants.note_to_tdpo: Same ramp but with weather beam-on to the vessel. Saturation will occur earlier. Compare the result to your head-on ramp.

tasks.title: Current Vector Analysis
tasks.setup: Set calm wind and wave. Add only current at 0.5kts from 090 degrees. Allow 10 minutes for model to fully settle before recording anything.
tasks.execute: After 10 minutes, record the current vector displayed by the DP system. Compare the displayed value to the actual current you set. Then add wind at 15kts from 180 degrees — directly opposing current. Observe how the displayed current vector changes over 5 minutes. Record the new value. Explain the difference.
professional_standard: Correctly record displayed vs set current values
Observe and record change when wind added
Correctly explain why displayed current changed when wind was added
Understand that DP current vector represents all unmodelled forces

How does this understanding affect how you interpret the current vector during a real operation?

variants.title: Current Vector in Complex Environment
variants.note_to_tdpo: Add all three environmental forces and analyse the current vector. How much of what you see is tidal current vs wind vs wave force?

tasks.title: Model Corruption and Recovery
tasks.setup: Moderate environment set and settled. Vessel on DP at datum. Note current vector value before starting.
tasks.execute: Run 1 — Corrupted transition: Make an aggressive 300m JSMH transit with large inputs and abrupt stops. Immediately select DP. Record thruster behaviour and current vector for 2 minutes. Note time to settle. Run 2 — Clean transition: Reset. Make the same 300m transit but slow to near zero before selecting Monitor briefly, then DP. Record settle time and capture quality. Compare both runs.
professional_standard: Observe measurable difference in capture quality between runs
Correctly identify current vector corruption after aggressive transit
Explain the mechanism of model corruption
Record settle time difference between methods

variants.note_to_tdpo: A much larger transit produces much greater corruption. This simulates moving between rigs. Notice how much longer the model takes to settle.
